To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of highly doped absorber material and reduction of absorber thickness is an efficient way to achieve both high detectivity and subnanosecond response time in zero-bias operation mode of a long-wavelength infrared photodiode.
the time constant of an HgCdTe infrared detector is inversely proportional to the thickness of the absorber layer.
a highly doped p-HgCdTe photodetector with a very thin absorber layer is the best candidate for fast-response long-wavelength infrared photodetectors operating in zero-bias configuration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of device design for fast response and high detectivity in zero-bias operation mode.
the design of HgCdTe detectors that can achieve both high detectivity and high speed of operation in zero-bias operation mode.
optimization of device parameters to achieve fast response in zero-bias operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zero-bias operation mode is feasible for HgCdTe detectors with a time constant of 0.1 ns or less.
the design of the photodiode should be tailored to the specific application.
zero-bias photodiodes with subnanosecond response times and high detectivity can be achieved by optimizing the device parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the zero-bias photodiodes with absorber thickness less than 4 μms and highly doped absorber (NA = 1 × 1017 cm3) are the best choices for fast response and high detectivity.
zero-bias operation mode can be a viable option for HgCdTe infrared photodiodes with proper design.

a zero-bias long-wavelength infrared photodiode with subnanosecond response and high detectivity can be achieved by using a highly doped absorber with thickness below 4–5 μm and an optically immersed structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a photodiode with time response below 1  ns can be realized at 230 K with zero bias and with detectivity exceeding 1 × 109 cmHz1/2/W. The
zero-bias operation mode of photodiodes is feasible with fast response time and high detectivity.
a fast and sensitive photodiode can be realized by optimizing the doping concentration of the absorber layer and the absorber thickness.
